text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected for /v1/generate on dedicated-us-west pool. Current p99: 9.8s (SLO 5s). Streaming stalls and increased queue depth observed. Paging oncall.

kiran: @here I'm oncall. Investigating. Which customers impacted? any running canaries?

emily: Seeing 3 customers complaining via support: Acme, Brainwave. Both reporting timeouts on long streaming responses. Customer threads: https://support.internal/ACME-427

sara: Dashboard shows queue_depth spike from ~50 -> 120 at 16:04 UTC, warmup rate flat. Autoscaler didn't add nodes for ~3m. p95 jumped to 2.1s, p99 to 9.8s. Streaming stalls correlate with high KV cache misses.

diego: Adding context: we deployed a model variant yesterday that has larger KV footprints. The autoscaler policy has a warmup_limit of 2 nodes/min to avoid thrash. Looks like burst >> warmup capacity.

kiran: Ok. Immediate mitigations: 1) fall back affected routes to smaller model variant; 2) temporarily raise autoscaler warmup rate if safe; 3) enable manual scale-up to absorb backlog. Who can run those?

diego: I can trigger manual scale. Command:
```
ops-scale --pool dedicated-us-west --add 8 --reason "incident 1868004321 manual absorb"
```
But that takes ~90s to spin up and warm caches. We should also route traffic to spare region or fallback model.

sara: Suggest reducing concurrency per worker for streaming to reduce tail latency while nodes spin up:
```
set-pool-config --pool dedicated-us-west --max-concurrency 8
```
Will push in 30s.

kiran: Emily, notify customers about transient failures and mitigation steps. Robin, any product constraints on fallback model for Acme/Brainwave?

emily: Sending messages: "We're seeing elevated latencies on streaming. We're routing you to a compatible model variant and scaling capacity — expected recovery ~5-8 minutes. Will follow up." :phone: I'll paste updates in CS threads.

robin: Fallback to the smaller model is acceptable for both customers; quality drop is small for their prompts. Approve.

incident-bot: @kiran Incident created: INC-2026-1868004321. Severity: Sev2. Paging routed to oncall and SRE runbook.

sara: Pushed concurrency reduction. Monitoring now. Queue depth stopped rising but backlog remains ~90k tokens in-flight. p99 dropped to 6.5s after concurrency change.

diego: Manual scale command executed. New instances starting. Logs show warmup tasks for KV cache fetches:
```
[worker-12] kv_warmup: fetching 3.2M keys
[worker-12] model_load: quantized weights loaded
```
Warmup throughput ~30s per replica for first prefix-heavy workloads.

kiran: Can we short-circuit streaming by enabling prefix caching for common system prompts? Any quick toggles?

diego: We can enable prefix cache hotlist for top 50 prefixes. Doing it now.

sara: After hotlist enable + manual scale, p99 back to 3.0s, p95 ~1.5s. Streaming stalls still occasional but much reduced. Queue depth dropping steadily.

emily: Customer update posted: reduced to fallback model + we've scaled capacity. "We expect normal service in ~4-6 minutes." They asked for ETA on root cause.

kiran: Initial hypothesis: dedicated pool saturation due to an unexpected burst of long-sequence requests from a few tenants combined with a recent model variant that increased KV footprint; autoscaler warmup limits prevented catching up fast enough.

robin: Is this reproducible? Can we add a guard to detect sudden KV-heavy model deployments or restrict model variants per pool during business hours?

diego: Actionable items: (1) adjust autoscaler to allow emergency burst scale beyond warmup_limit when queue_depth > X AND median_seq_len > Y, (2) add model-onboarding check to estimate KV footprint and update pool tagging, (3) improve cache warmup parallelism.

sara: Also add runbook step: when p99>5s and queue_depth>100 trigger manual scale and fallback route in one-click.

incident-bot: NOTE: incident handoff scheduled at 16:25 UTC to next oncall.

kiran: I'll handoff to @sara in 20m. Next steps for now: monitor until p99 < 2s for 10 min. Diego, leave scale up running until headroom restored.

diego: Leaving +8 nodes live and autoscaler limits temporarily relaxed for this pool. I'll file PR for burst policy.

emily: CS will follow up with affected customers with incident summary and remediation timeline.

sara: Logging actions for postmortem. Collecting metrics: queue_depth, autoscale_events, model_variant_id, kv_miss_rate, p95/p99 over the incident window.

kiran: Good work. If anything regresses ping me. I'll update INC ticket and Slack channel with timeline.

sara: Marking incident as mitigated at 16:37 UTC. p99 stabilized at 1.8s. We'll keep monitoring.

emily: Customers acknowledged and are okay with the fallback for now.

kiran: Postmortem owners: diego (root cause + autoscaler changes), sara (runbook + observability), emily (customer comms). Deadline: draft in 72 hours. :memo:

incident-bot: Closing note: cleanup tasks: revert temporary autoscaler relax in 24h if PR not merged, keep added nodes until autoscaler rebalanced.
